description.sr_latin: Nadimci, komplimenti i poruke za tvoju dragu osobu.
description.en: Pet names, compliments, and sweet messages for your special person.

phrases.context: The most common Serbian pet name. You'll hear this constantly between couples.
phrases.notes: 'Duša' means soul — calling someone 'dušo' is like saying they are your soul. Vocative case.

phrases.context: Very warm and natural. Used freely in conversation, not just romantic moments.
phrases.notes: Vocative of 'ljubav' (love). Can be used on its own or combined: 'Ljubavi moja.'

phrases.context: Affectionate but slightly more formal than 'dušo'. Works in public without being too cheesy.
phrases.notes: Use 'dragi' when speaking to a man.

phrases.context: Playful and flirty. Like calling someone 'babe' in English but cuter.
phrases.notes: From 'maca' (female cat). Very common among younger couples.

phrases.context: Cute and playful. Usually for guys but not exclusively.
phrases.notes: From 'medved' (bear). 'Medo' is the diminutive — think teddy bear, not grizzly.

phrases.context: Very sweet and warm. Also used for kids. Not cheesy — Serbs actually say this a lot.
phrases.notes: Sunce = sun. The possessive 'moje' makes it personal.

phrases.context: Common term of endearment. Not over the top — parents use it for kids too.
phrases.notes: Zlato = gold. Very natural in everyday Serbian.

phrases.context: Deeply affectionate. Feels sincere, not performative.
phrases.notes: Srce = heart. One of the most emotionally loaded pet names.

phrases.context: Direct and sincere. Use when she's dressed up or you just feel it.
phrases.notes: 'Pre-' is an intensifier prefix. 'Lepa' = pretty, 'prelepa' = stunning/gorgeous.

phrases.context: When she's trying on clothes, wearing something new, or got a haircut.
phrases.notes: Literally 'it stands nicely on you.' Works for clothes, hair, accessories — anything.

phrases.en: You killed it! / You look amazing!
phrases.context: Casual, high-energy compliment. Like 'slaaay' vibes.
phrases.notes: Literally 'you killed (it).' Slang but widely used. Very natural among young people.

phrases.context: Genuine compliment. 'Baš' adds emphasis — like 'really' or 'truly.'
phrases.notes: 'Baš' is one of the most useful Serbian words. It adds sincerity or emphasis.

phrases.context: When she makes you laugh. 'Mnogo' = very/so much.
phrases.notes: 'Smešna' for a woman, 'smešan' for a man.

phrases.context: Simple but powerful. Good after she does something nice or just because.
phrases.notes: 'Naj-' prefix makes superlatives. Dobar → najbolji/najbolja.

phrases.context: The go-to 'I miss you.' Natural over text or in person.
phrases.notes: Literally 'you are missing to me.' The subject is the person you miss, not you.

phrases.context: Sweet mid-day text. Not too heavy, just right.
phrases.notes: 'Mislim' = I think. 'Na tebe' = about you.

phrases.en: I can't wait to see you.
phrases.context: Before a date or when you haven't seen each other in a while.
phrases.notes: 'Jedva čekam' literally means 'I barely wait' — used for eager anticipation.

phrases.context: The big one. Serbs don't throw this around casually — it carries weight.
phrases.notes: Unlike English, there's no casual 'love ya.' This is always sincere.

phrases.context: Perfect morning text. Warm without being over the top.
phrases.notes: 'Jutro' = morning. Can swap 'sunce' for any pet name.

phrases.context: Classic goodnight text. Feels natural and caring.
phrases.notes: 'Laku noć' is the standard goodnight. Adding a pet name makes it personal.

phrases.context: Flirty goodnight message. Playful, not desperate.
phrases.notes: 'Sanjati' = to dream. Imperative form here.

phrases.context: Caring goodnight. Feels warm and protective.
phrases.notes: 'Spavaj' = sleep (imperative). 'Lepo' = nicely/well.

phrases.en: I always have time for you.
phrases.context: Smooth and genuine. Works as a text reply when she asks if you're busy.
phrases.notes: 'Uvek' = always. 'Vremena' = time (genitive case).

phrases.context: Playful guilt trip. Used when she's teasing or might cancel plans.
phrases.notes: 'Nemoj' = don't (informal imperative). Keeps it light.

phrases.context: A bit cheesy but delivered with a smile, it works. Serbs appreciate directness.
phrases.notes: 'Ukrala' = stole (feminine past tense). 'Ukrao' for masculine.

phrases.sr_latin: Srećan sam kad sam s tobom.
phrases.sr_cyrillic: Срећан сам кад сам с тобом.
phrases.en: I'm happy when I'm with you.
phrases.context: Sincere and simple. Good for a quiet moment together.
phrases.notes: 'Srećan' = happy (masculine). 'Srećna' for a woman saying this.

variations.sr_latin: Srećna sam kad sam s tobom.
variations.sr_cyrillic: Срећна сам кад сам с тобом.
variations.en: I'm happy when I'm with you. (said by a woman)

phrases.context: Heavy but genuine. Save for real moments.
phrases.notes: 'Sve' = everything. 'Značiti' = to mean.

phrases.context: Passionate but casual. Common expression, not as intense as it sounds in English.
phrases.notes: 'Luditi' = to go crazy. 'Za tobom' = for/after you.

phrases.context: When she's stressed or upset. Simple and comforting.
phrases.notes: 'Tu' = here. Direct and supportive.

phrases.context: Comforting someone who's worried or going through something tough.
phrases.notes: 'Će' = will (future tense marker). 'U redu' = in order / okay.

phrases.context: Gentle reassurance. The pet name softens it.
phrases.notes: 'Brinuti' = to worry. 'Ne brini' = don't worry (informal).

phrases.en: Sorry, I didn't mean it like that.
phrases.context: After you said something wrong or it came out badly.
phrases.notes: 'Izvini' = sorry/excuse me (informal). 'Nisam mislio' = I didn't think/mean.

variations.en: Sorry, I didn't mean it like that. (said by a woman)

phrases.context: De-escalation move. Shows you'd rather be close than right.
phrases.notes: 'Hajde' = come on / let's. 'Svađati se' = to argue/fight.

phrases.context: Vulnerable and honest. Good way to break a tense silence.
phrases.notes: 'Mrzim' = I hate. 'Kad' = when.
